name: pdk-imessage-conversation-analyzer-dataframe
instr:
The reaction numbers ica gives me are off for my newer conversations. When someone takes back a tapback, the "Removed a heart from …" line counts as a message, and when someone changes a heart to a thumbs up, both count. A friend's phone is set to Spanish, so their tapbacks count as messages, and a reply I typed as Loved “Dune” counts as a reaction.

The messages frame from `ica.get_dataframes()` should match what the conversation shows in Messages today. `is_reaction` should be true for exactly the tapbacks, whatever language their text is in, and also when a row has no text. Only tapbacks that are still showing should be rows: each person has at most one tapback on a message, the one they left last, and a tapback they took back is gone. The removal lines are never rows. This has to hold with a date range too: a tapback that was changed or taken back after the end of the range doesn't count, and the range itself keeps working as it does now. `message_totals` and the other analyzers read that frame.

A copy of my Messages database is at /data/Library/Messages/chat.db, with my Contacts database under /data/Library, laid out as in my home folder. Databases from older macOS versions that don't record tapback details should keep working as they do today, and the checks in /app/AGENTS.md should still pass. There's no network here; the project's dependencies, ruff and ty are installed in /opt/venv.
